title: Wordwood
tagline: Follow Warden Wren through a wood where the trees are words and the paths are sentences: how computers split, count, tag, remember and weigh language.

funFacts.text: The first published stemmer, a program that chops word endings, was written in 1968. A later one by Martin Porter, published in 1980, became the standard for English.
The Viterbi algorithm is named after Andrew Viterbi, who proposed it in 1967 to decode signals sent over noisy links. It is now also used to tag words in sentences.
The word2vec method for learning word vectors was presented in 2013 by researchers at Google.
The 2017 paper that introduced the transformer was called 'Attention Is All You Need'.
